chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Frequent the Tahleel (declaring the Oneness of God) and the Takbeer (declaring the Greatness of God), for there is nothing more beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than the Tahleel and the Takbeer.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِير: Takbeer: The declaration of the Greatness of God (Allahu Akbar)
key_terms.التَّهْلِيل: Tahleel: The declaration of the Oneness of God (La ilaha illallah)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Azza wa Jalla: The Mighty and Majestic (an honorific for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved act to Allah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) emphasizes the supreme merit of dhikr by declaring that Tahleel and Takbeer are the most beloved acts to Allah, a statement that underscores their foundational role in Shia devotional practice. This narration is often cited by scholars to highlight the spiritual efficacy of simple, frequent verbal remembrance as a means of drawing closer to the Divine, reinforcing the concept that sincerity in declaration outweighs complex rituals.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘I heard himasws saying: ‘Frequent from the Tahleel (extollation of the Oneness), and the Takbeer (Exclamation of the Greatness), for there is nothing more Beloved to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic than the Tahleel and the Takbeer’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad from Rib’ I from Fudayl who has said the following: “I heard one of the two Imam (a.s.) (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah) saying, ‘Increase al- Tahlil and al-Takbir, there is nothing more beloved to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, than al-Tahlil and al-Takbir , ’”
